meta.method: curl -sSL (Chrome UA) -> snapshots-official/<slug>.raw.html -> fetch_official.py stdlib HTML-to-text -> snapshots-official/<slug>.txt. Every quote with a `snapshot` must be an exact substring of that .txt (check: node check_official.mjs). Quotes may contain \n where the page puts the items in separate blocks.

status_legend.VERIFIED: number appears verbatim on an official government page, fetched raw, quote is a substring of the local snapshot
status_legend.†: only readable via a summarising fetch (WebFetch); no local snapshot; check by hand

meta.alias_boundary: Alias regexes use explicit letter-class lookarounds [A-Za-zÀ-ÖØ-öø-ÿ] instead of \b, because \b fails after a trailing accented letter (e.g. /\bcanad[áa]\b/i does not match 'Canadá?'), and avoid \p{L}/u for Hermes portability (UNKNOWN whether the target runtime supports Unicode property escapes).
meta.excluded_sources: No Wikipedia, no news. Nothing under blind/ or rnd/veil/ was read.

engine_alias_bugs_found: /\b(canada|canad[áa])\b/i misses 'Canadá' followed by space/punctuation (\b after a non-ASCII letter). Same pattern risk for any alias ending in an accented letter.
/\b(turkey|t[üu]rkiye|turquia)\b/i matches the food ('choked on a turkey bone') — emergencyNumbersLine() scans arbitrary text, so a food mention attaches Turkey's numbers.
